text.p: Following are the main stories from Slovenia's Thursday morning newspapers:
- The union of Slovenian railway workers, which entered its 10th day of striking, refused to continue talks unless the management withdraws suspensions of strike leaders.
- State Council, the upper house of parliament, vetoed the lower house's decision to introduce tax on new cars, saying the new law would be discriminatory towards disabled persons.
- Parliament adopted the new law on telecommunications and road traffic safety.
- Slovenia will issue a 400 million mark seven-year eurobond on June 16. Joint lead managers of the issue are Dresdner Kleinwort Benson and Credit Suisse First Boston.
